title: ⭐⭐ Revision: reading an interview and answering it

questions.prompt: Your cousin cannot stop talking about football. Which sentence describes him in correct English?

options.text: My cousin is obsessed of football and knows every player.
My cousin is obsessed to football and plays it every Sunday.
My cousin is obsessed with football and talks about nothing else.
My cousin obsesses football and watches every match on TV.

questions.explanation: "My cousin is obsessed with football and talks about nothing else." is correct: obsessed travels with the preposition with, and the second half of the sentence shows what an obsession looks like. "obsessed to" and "obsessed of" copy prepositions from other verbs, and "My cousin obsesses football and watches every match on TV." uses obsess as if it took a direct object, which it does not in this sense.

questions.prompt: One question of the questionnaire asks whether pocket money is a right or a favour. Which answer treats it as a right?

options.text: Parents give it only to the children who work hard.
Parents give it when they can, and I always thank them for it.
Parents keep it and buy what the children need.
Parents must give it: it is part of what a child is owed.

questions.explanation: "Parents must give it: it is part of what a child is owed." treats pocket money as a right, because a right is something owed to you, with must and no condition attached. "Parents give it when they can, and I always thank them for it." is the favour answer, and thanking is its sign. "Parents give it only to the children who work hard." makes it a reward, and "Parents keep it and buy what the children need." removes pocket money altogether.

questions.prompt: Your group has agreed on one thing it likes about Carol. Which sentence gives that opinion in correct English?

options.text: I am feeling that she has stayed simple in spite of her money.
I feel about her simple life in spite of all her money now.
I feel she to stay simple in spite of all the money she has.
I feel that she has stayed simple in spite of her money.

questions.explanation: "I feel that she has stayed simple in spite of her money." is correct: feel is followed by that and a whole sentence, and it stays in the present simple because it names a state of mind. "I am feeling that..." puts a state verb into the progressive. "I feel she to stay simple..." replaces the clause with an infinitive that has no place there, and "I feel about her simple life..." uses a preposition that belongs to feel about somebody, not to giving an opinion.

questions.prompt: The newspapers present Carol and Max as a couple. What does the interview tell the reader about the two of them?

options.text: They have been friends since they were small.
They have decided to marry after her album.
They have not spoken to each other for a year.
They met on the set of her first video.

questions.explanation: "They have been friends since they were small." is what Carol answers, and it corrects the newspapers rather than confirming them. "They met on the set of her first video." invents a meeting the interview never mentions. "They have decided to marry after her album." repeats the story she denies, and "They have not spoken to each other for a year." goes too far in the other direction: she does not break with him, she says what the friendship is.

questions.prompt: Carol answers a journalist with this sentence: "I'm not a skinny girl but I don't mind that." Which question was she asked?

options.text: You have your own house. What do you spend your money on?
Your mother travels with you. Is she the closest person to you?
Newspapers talk a lot about your looks. What do you think of that?
Some people say show business is a ruthless world. Do you agree?

questions.explanation: "Newspapers talk a lot about your looks. What do you think of that?" is the one: the answer describes her body and then gives her opinion of it, which is exactly the two halves the question asks for. The question about show business would be answered with an opinion on a trade, the question about spending with the name of a purchase, and the question about her mother with a yes or a no. None of those shapes fits an answer about being skinny.

questions.prompt: Your group is writing its short report on three things it does not like about Carol. Which sentence belongs in that report?

options.text: The interview appeared in a British newspaper.
We do not like the way she speaks about her parents' house.
Carol Chapel was born seventeen years ago in a British town.
Show business is known to be a ruthless world for everybody.

questions.explanation: "We do not like the way she speaks about her parents' house." belongs there: a report of opinions says what the group thinks, in the first person plural, about one precise point. The three others are facts, and a fact can be copied from the text by anybody without an opinion being formed. The classic trap is the last one, which sounds like a judgement but only repeats Carol's own words about her trade.
